clue.text: Painter with urge to action at breakfast

parts.note: Francis Bacon was a British painter
and is a plain synonym for with
to egg someone on is to urge them to act

explanation.surface: An artist is keen to get moving over the morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried rashers served with a fried hen's egg make a classic British morning plate.

clue.text: Settle degree in jousting

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
a lance is the long weapon used in jousting

explanation.surface: A knight's rank is decided by how he fares in a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: To balance an account is to settle it so both columns agree.

clue.text: Throws out players!

explanation.surface: Someone ejects the actors from the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman casts a line, throwing it out; the casts of plays are their companies of actors.

clue.text: See 19 across
Commonsense of we French?

explanation.surface: A question whether the French have good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical wit or gumption is a sense of nous; in French the first person plural pronoun is nous.

clue.text: Come forth with Bible suddenly appearing

parts.note: to emerge is to come forth
NT is the New Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone steps out clutching scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emergent is just coming into view or being, newly arising.

clue.text: Force us to zeal

parts.note: g is the symbol for the force of gravity

explanation.surface: An order pushing a group into enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment and eagerness, much like zeal.

clue.text: Mark of no advantage

explanation.surface: A sign that something brings no benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch is a small mark or graze; a scratch player in golf has no handicap, so no strokes given.

clue.text: Affable about east plan

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is friendly on the subject of an eastern scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant person is agreeable and friendly company.

clue.text: Faintness of girl with something due to change

parts.note: it stands for some unnamed thing

indicators.note: to change means the letters of the word due are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman feels weak because some debt is about to alter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is weariness and lack of energy, a languid faintness.

clue.text: Doh-ray-me up to eclipse we hear!

annotationWithheld.why: Doh-ray-me up to eclipse we hear! (5): SOLAR; no sound parse found: 'Doh-ray-me up' may suggest SOH LAH aloud, but 'to eclipse' cannot define an adjective and the clue may be misprinted
annotationWithheld.clue: Doh-ray-me up to eclipse we hear!

clue.text: Wise old Greek in Troy home alternative!

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A Greek sage at Troy is offered a house or something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestor was the aged, sagacious king of Pylos who counselled the Greeks at the siege of Troy.

clue.text: Don't know nothing in ranting round!

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for nothing goes inside the shuffled word
round suggests the word ranting is turned about into a new order

parts.note: O, the zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone admits to no knowledge in the middle of a round of shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't know' is a phrase standing for an adjective: someone who doesn't know is uninformed. 'round' gives IGNRANT, and 'in' places the zero within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be uninformed is to lack knowledge: those who don't know are unaware.

clue.text: Replacement from players at Zurich

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is drawn out of the run of letters in the next words

explanation.surface: A substitute arrives from the sportsmen at a Swiss city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior substitute, a stand-in for the real thing.

clue.text: Uneasy about ones to question?

explanation.surface: A detective is troubled about whom to interview.
explanation.definitionFit: If one suspects something one is uneasy about it; suspects are people police wish to interview.

clue.text: Fresh corn with each move over boundary

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters of corn and each are made anew in another order

explanation.surface: A farmer carries new grain past the edge of a field.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to intrude beyond proper limits onto another's ground.

clue.text: Emphasise about working as police officer say?

parts.note: a police officer works in the force; in force also means operating

explanation.surface: Someone stresses a point about serving as a constable.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce a point is to strengthen and stress it.

clue.text: Bone is mostly old keyboard instrument!

annotationWithheld.why: Bone is mostly old keyboard instrument! (8): CLAVICLE; no instrument found whose shortened form gives CLAVICLE (CLAVICHORD trimmed gives CLAVICHOR), so the clue may be misprinted
annotationWithheld.clue: Bone is mostly old keyboard instrument!

clue.text: Relatively like a nun?

parts.note: relatively hints at a family member, while a nun is addressed by a title of kinship

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a person behaves rather like a member of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisterly means befitting a female sibling, and nuns are called Sister.

clue.text: Extraordinarily cedes about London University to denote achievement

definitions.note: a noun defining a verb: to have achievement

indicators.note: about tells us the shuffled letters wrap around the abbreviation for the college
extraordinarily suggests the letters of cedes are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: UC is University College, part of London University

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly gives up on a college in the capital to mark success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinarily' gives SCEED, and 'about' wraps those letters round the college; the definition is loose, since to succeed is to attain an achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed is to achieve one's aim, attaining success.

clue.text: Tenth I holed in heath a different way to be exact

indicators.note: a different way says the letters of the preceding words are arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A golfer sinks the tenth hole on a moorland course by an unusual route.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' just before 'different way' is part of the fodder, supplying the second A.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be precisely right, landing the blow squarely.

clue.text: Me, in the end, will hesitate to be the one to make alterations

indicators.note: in tells us one word goes inside the other

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone vows to pause before finally making changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end' looks like a phrase meaning finally, but it simply supplies its own word, which 'in' then wraps around ME.
explanation.definitionFit: One who emends corrects or revises texts.

clue.text: React strangely to my possessing imagination in the making

indicators.note: strangely suggests the letters of react are placed in an odd order

parts.note: I've is short for I have, said of what I possess

explanation.surface: Someone responds oddly to having a vivid fancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Creative describes having inventive ideas, using original thought to produce things.

clue.text: Characteristic of the turncoat with no alternative

indicators.note: with no tells us a word is removed from the longer one

explanation.surface: A defector's typical feature is having no other choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing quality or feature.

clue.text: Obliterate notes on a card

parts.note: E, F and F are musical notes
an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: Someone scrawls over the writing on a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface is to rub out or erase completely.

clue.text: Takes from easy ethical extract up to now

indicators.note: takes from says the answer is drawn out of the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone quotes from a simple moral passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extract' is the noun the hidden letters form, part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: As yet means so far, until the present time.

clue.text: See 19 across
Former rat changed run

indicators.note: changed means the letters of rat are reordered

explanation.surface: A reformed scoundrel took off.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide or bye.

clue.text: Scatter observed sign of discernment

parts.note: to clear a crowd is to scatter it
eyed means looked at or observed

explanation.surface: A crowd disperses after spotting a portent.
explanation.definitionFit: Being clear-eyed shows sharp insight and realistic judgment.

clue.text: Fashion with dog offering new directions

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gundog

explanation.surface: A stylish hound points the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A trendsetter leads others in new styles, giving fashion a fresh course.
